newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures slipped back from a new contract high as Bunds and U.S. bonds failed to hold their gains, while a growing feeling that the strong dollar could delay rate cuts led to a flattening of the curve.

The March bond future rallied to set a new high of 131.16 early in the session with relief that Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan did not surprise markets and an Italian rate cut buoying the market.
Traders said, however, the movements were being driven largely by technical factors and that there was a certain amount of caution above 131. The contract settled at 130.80, up 0.26.

Analysts said the most significant move of the day was the flattening of the curve. They said the curve had been flattening slightly during the past few days but the trend accelerated on Wednesday with the area up to four-years suffering most.
The gap between two- and 30-year French government bond yields narrowed nine basis points. The 30-year area of the curve outperformed the 10-year area as well.
"The short end got a bit impatient with waiting on lower short-term rates, it was not happening nearly as quickly as they had hoped," Joanne Perez, strategist at Merrill Lynch in Paris said.
"Effectively, with the dollar so strong, there's a growing belief that it will stop rates going down in Europe," Iain Lindsay, senior bond analyst at Credit Lyonnais said.

The franc fell as low as 5.5453 against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday, the lowest it's been since June 16, 1994. So far this year the franc has tumbled 6.9 percent and is 13.6 percent weaker than its lowest level last year.
Traders said there had been some buying in the 10-year area by domestics and that longer-dated bonds where also attracting investors moving along the curve to look for higher yields.
Analysts said the underperformance at the front of the curve had petered out by the April 2004 OAT, which is the cheapest to deliver bond into the March bond future.
One trader said a five percent yield on the cheapest to deliver bond was a target being eyed by futures traders. It fell to 5.12 percent on Wednesday.

The four-year area of the curve also suffered slightly from the sale of 10 billion francs of October 2000 bonds by French welfare debt repayment fund CADES at a spread of six basis points over the October 2000 BTAN.

Perez also said the long end of the French curve was helped by the impression that Europe was partly protected from the United States because of the disparity in the state of economic growth in the two areas.

She said, however, that the negative spread between core European yields and U.S. bonds, boosted by traditional January buying by investors was nearing dangerous levels. "The over exuberant January effect could prove expensive in February."
A primary dealer at a French bank said flows were still fairly limited and the full effect of domestic buying had yet to be seen which could help support the market in due course.
A mutual fund manager also said he did not think the full force of buying by domestic investors had been reached yet.
The 10-year spread between French and German bond yields moved out to minus 20 basis points from minus 16 on Tuesday.
One victim of the curve flattening on Wednesday was the TEC 10 variable rate OAT which benefits especially from steepening between 10 and 30 year bonds.
The margin on the variable rate bond below the TEC 10 index fell to 140 from 146 basis points on Tuesday. It has been as high as 151 basis points recently.
-- David Clarke, Paris Newsroom +331 4221 5542
